newsitem.title: UK: UK government orders clampdown on IRA prisoners.
newsitem.headline: UK government orders clampdown on IRA prisoners.

text.p: The British government on Thursday ordered a security clampdown on IRA prisoners who tried to tunnel out of the Maze prison in Northern Ireland.

Prison authorities at the weekend discovered an elaborately constructed tunnel at the Maze, where warders had been accused of allowing Irish Republican Army prisoners to run what amounted to "no go" areas inside the jail.
The Northern Ireland prison service said security at the Belfast jail would be stepped up, with inmates subject to regular headcounts.
High-risk IRA prisoners would be locked in their cells overnight and access to gym, handicraft and computer facilities would be withdrawn.
The government was severely embarrassed by the tunnel built by IRA prisoners, who are opposed to British rule in Northern Ireland.
The tunnel was lit by electric wiring removed from the prison and rubble cleared from the shaft was stored in prison cells.
